vo.text: A new car. A year's pay. Gone already.
About $78,000 a second, every second, all year.
The debt grew $2.46 trillion in fiscal 2026.
Now a whole working life of median pay.

verdict.text:
A whole working life
in **≈ 33 seconds**

notes: Stress variant: captions off (the label stack sits in the caption band), 6 milestones (two of them 0.19 s apart), a long two-line label, a label without an amount, frame 1 already 0.4 s into the count (counterT[0] = -0.4, so the header says 'in real time', not 'since you hit play'), no lookOpts. Maths: rate = $2,460,000,000,000 ÷ 31,536,000 s = $78,006.09 a second (shown ≈ $78,000). Counting time to each milestone = value ÷ 78,006.09: car $50,089 → 0.642 s; pay $65,052 → 0.834 s; house $393,700 → 5.047 s; $650,520 → 8.339 s; $1,000,000 → 12.820 s; $2,602,080 (= $1,251 × 52 × 40) → 33.357 s (≈ 33 s, the verdict). Video time = counting time − 0.4 s. Frame 1 reads 78,006.09 × 0.4 = $31,202. Counter end 33.0 s → 78,006.09 × 33.4 = 2,605,403.4 → ≈ $2,605,403. Sources (as verified in teasers/v2/10-cost-counter.md, 10b): FY2026 debt growth $2.46T (Treasury Debt to the Penny via PrimeRates; GAO and Euronews consistency checks); average new-vehicle transaction price Aug 2026 $50,089 (Cox Automotive / KBB, 2026-09-10); BLS median full-time pay $1,251 a week (Q2 2026); Census median new house $393,700 (Aug 2026). The debt grows in steps (auctions, tax dates): this is the year's average rate.
